title: Zero-downtime migration conductor and compatibility matrix for Private
creator: Sofia Park
description:
Overview:
We need a migration conductor for Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) that performs orchestrated, zero-downtime platform upgrades across control-plane and data-plane components. This ticket scopes a conductor service + operator CLI + compatibility matrix generator that: (1) computes safe upgrade paths across LTS channels and minor/patch versions; (2) coordinates DB schema migrations with logical translators to avoid incompatible reads/writes; (3) performs staged node rollouts with programmable gates; (4) provides preflight probes and a dry-run mode for customers; (5) emits deterministic telemetry and rollback markers for incident analysis.

Goals:
- Provide a binary/service (migration-conductor) that customer operators can run in their Private control plane to orchestrate upgrades end-to-end.
- Generate a version compatibility matrix that maps code version, DB schema version, and runtime artifact compatibility (e.g., agent protocol, query plan).
- Implement zero-downtime transactional migration path for critical stateful services (auth-store, user-config, model-index) using logical replication + read-side translators.
- Surface clear rollout gates and automation hooks: canary percentage, health-signal thresholds, autoscale-safety check, KV cache warmup hooks.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not build a new heavy-duty schema migration DSL. We'll reuse the existing migration runner and add orchestrator adapters.
- Does not include new model binary format changes (separate model-onboarding project).

Design summary / proposal:
- Migration conductor has three subcomponents: Planner, Orchestrator, and Safeguard Agent.
  - Planner: validates desired target version against a compatibility matrix and emits an ordered plan of steps (preflight -> canary -> cohort -> full).
  - Orchestrator: executes plan across cluster resources using the existing private control-plane RPC; supports concurrency limits and maintenance windows.
  - Safeguard Agent: lightweight per-node agent to perform pre-upgrade checks (disk, KV-coldness, model cache status) and to accept/emit probe results.
- DB path: use logical snapshot + transactional apply for schema changes that are not backward compatible. Steps: create logical snapshot, deploy read-translator layer (feature-flagged), migrate writes to new schema via dual-writes if required, promote new schema, then garbage-collect translator.
- Rollout gates: health pass (5m rolling), latency regression (<10% p95), error rate delta (<0.5%), KV miss ratio <2%, disk headroom >15%. Any gate violation triggers automatic pause and optional rollback.
- LTS awareness: Planner picks upgrade path that minimizes intermediate steps by consulting LTS channels; allows skip-to-lts when allowed by compatibility matrix and security policy.

Runbook / Steps (high level):
1) Preflight: run `conductor check --target <version>` creating deterministic plan; run in dry-run mode to collect probes.
2) Staging canary: apply to 2 nodes (1 control, 1 data-plane) for 30 minutes under elevated telemetry.
3) Cohorts: rollout to cohorts (20%, 50%, 100%) with automated gates and manual approval point after 50%.
4) Post-upgrade verification: run smoke tests, query consistency checks, KV cache warmup verification, and cost telemetry baseline comparison.
5) Rollback: orchestrator supports stepwise rollback to last known-good version and replays rollback-migration transcript.

Telemetry and alerts:
- Emit structured events for each plan-step (plan.create, step.start, step.success, step.pause, step.abort, step.rollback).
- Metrics: plan_duration_seconds, step_duration_seconds, gate_violations_total, rollback_count_total, canary_error_rate, cohort_latency_delta.
- Prebuilt dashboards: Upgrade Overview, Node-level Upgrade Timeline, Canary Failure Investigations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Planner can generate an upgrade plan between any two supported versions and export steps as JSON.
- Orchestrator successfully runs a dry-run plan against an existing onprem staging cluster without changing state.
- End-to-end canary upgrade (3-node staging) completes with no customer-facing downtime and meets gate thresholds.
- Compatibility matrix tool produces matrix CSV for every release and is included in release artifacts.
- Conductor supports an authenticated CLI with KMS/HSM integration for signing plan approvals.

Security & compliance notes:
- All plan execution events must be logged to customer audit logs with configurable retention and hashed signatures for non-repudiation.
- Security review required for KMS integration and plan-signing flow.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Dual-write introduces write amplification and potential divergence. Mitigation: add strong idempotency keys and reconciliation job with deterministic reconciliation window.
- Risk: Long-running migrations may increase disk usage. Mitigation: preflight disk delta calculator and mandatory autoscale guard.
- Risk: Customers with heavy custom integrations may experience compatibility gaps. Mitigation: expose 'compatibility-check' plugin hook that customers/devs can implement.

Next steps / implementation plan:
- Spike (3 days): implement compatibility-matrix generator and a Planner prototype that outputs step JSON.
- Iteration 1 (2 weeks): build Orchestrator with dry-run + canary path and Safeguard Agent skeleton.
- Iteration 2 (2 weeks): integrate DB logical snapshot flow and dual-write adapters.
- QA (1 week): run against private staging clusters and produce remediation playbook.
